This is exactly what is expected to happen," she said.Her remarks referred to the controversy surrounding the 2022 remission granted to 11 men convicted in the Bilkis Bano case, whose release had drawn widespread criticism after visuals emerged showing them being welcomed outside jail.Pradhan had announced his resignation on Saturday in a post on X, saying, "I have sent my resignation letter to the Prime Minister." He added, "I am pained to see the events of the past 10 days. This is not a matter of personal prestige for me."Following the protests over the alleged paper leak, the centre announced a series of measures to overhaul the examination system. On July 23, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the establishment of fast track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leak cases. The government has also constituted a high-powered committee on examination reforms and introduced legislative changes aimed at strengthening safeguards against examination malpractice.
Article Summary: Pradhan arrived at Parliament to chants of "Dharmendra Pradhan zindabad" Opposition MPs led by Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra staged a protest inside the Parliament complex. Opposition leaders also demanded that home minister Amit Shah apologise for police action against peaceful protesters.

Article Title: CRPF to conduct 'professional post-event assessment' of RAF action at student protests
Article Text:
CRPF to conduct 'professional post-event assessment'

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think about the involvement of students in protests for their rights? It's crucial for democracy. They should focus on studies. Protests can be counterproductive. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Central Reserve Police Force ( CRPF ) Director General Gyanendra Pratap Singh on Monday said the force would conduct a "professional post-event assessment" of the action taken by Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel during CJP-led student protests, following the conclusion of the agitation.Singh said the review would be carried out in line with the CRPF's standard procedure after major operational deployments, now that the protest has ended and demonstrators have dispersed."Now, since agitation has been called off, and assembled people have dispersed, we would make a professional post event assessment, like we do after every major assignment, and then let you know the view of the force headquarters," Singh told ANI.The statement comes amid protests by Opposition MPs, including Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, in the Parliament House complex on Monday over alleged "police brutality" against students during the NEET paper leak agitation.The Opposition has also demanded an apology from Union Home Minister Amit Shah.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi claimed that reports indicated AK-47 rifles had been used against students protesting in Bihar and alleged that hundreds of demonstrators had been arrested and booked under multiple FIRs.The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha demanded action against those responsible for the alleged attack on the students.The development comes after weeks of student protests led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which drew nationwide attention after activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the movement with a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar.Tensions escalated during the 'Sansad Chalo' march on July 20, when police allegedly used tear gas and lathi-charges to disperse protesters marching towards Parliament.Amid sustained protests, Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister, following which Pralhad Joshi assumed charge of the ministry on Sunday.
Article Summary: CRPF to conduct 'professional post-event assessment' of action taken by Rapid Action Force (RAF) during CJP-led student protests. Review will be carried out in line with the CRPF's standard procedure after major operational deployments.

Article Title: 'All are invited': Kejriwal announces 'National Town Hall against E20' on August 1
Article Text: NEW DELHI: AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal on Monday announced that the party will organise a 'National Town Hall against E20' in the national capital on August 1 to mobilise public support against ethanol-blended petrol.Addressing a press conference, Kejriwal said the meeting, to be held at the Constitution Club of India, will bring together experts, vehicle owners and members of the public to discuss concerns over E20 fuel."We are inviting people to join in large numbers this platform where we will discuss how to create pressure on the central government to withdraw the E20 petrol. Experts and people who have faced problems with their vehicles, all are invited," he said.Kejriwal said the AAP's online petition demanding that E20 fuel be made optional has received more than two lakh signatures."Next week, I will go to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's house with the online petition. But that would be after this meeting," the former Delhi chief minister said, urging the PM to address concerns before the issue grows into a nationwide agitation."The youth of this country have made an arrogant government bow down, resulting in Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.Now, I request the Prime Minister to also resolve the E20 issue before it turns into a massive protest," Kejriwal said.Announcing the town hall, he said people from Delhi-NCR could attend in person, while those from other parts of the country could participate online."We are starting a National Town Hall this Saturday afternoon to unite people on this issue. Residents of Delhi-NCR can attend in person, while those from outside can join online. We have provided a registration number (8588833212) for participants. Through this Town Hall, we will hold discussions with experts, victims, and the general public," he said.People wishing to participate virtually can send a message to 8588833212 to receive the online meeting link, he added.Kejriwal also criticised the alleged police action against protesting students in Bihar and other states saying, "This is not right. It makes the government appear dishonest and wavering in its stance."Commenting on the Centre's proposed anti-paper leak law, he questioned the government's "intent" rather than the legislation itself."Talk of such strict steps has been made before. If there is no intent to act against the mafia, no matter what law you make, it won't matter. Even the person arrested by the CBI was eventually released," he claimed.Responding to demands for the resignation of Punjab's education minister over allegations of paper leaks, Kejriwal defended the AAP government's record."We have been in power in Delhi for ten years, and not a single paper has leaked. Similarly, in Punjab, there hasn't been a single leak in the last five years. In one instance, two students tried to cheat using smart pens at two centres; they were caught immediately," he said.Highlighting Punjab's education performance, he added, "Before 2022, Punjab was ranked 27th in education; today, it is number one. This progress is what is bothering our opponents."Earlier this month, Kejriwal wrote to Prime Minister Modi seeking an appointment to discuss concerns over E20 fuel and urged the Centre to reduce the price of ethanol-blended petrol.In a post on X, he said, "When the youth of the country united and raised their voice, Dharmendra Pradhan had to resign. We will also have to unite and raise our voice against E20."Inviting people to the event, he added, "This Saturday, we are organizing the 'National Townhall Against E20', where you can share your views on E20 by participating. You can also join this online. All of you are invited. Date: 1 August, 2026. Time: 11:30 AM. Venue: Constitution Club, Delhi."
Article Summary: AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal announced that the party will organise a 'National Town Hall against E20' in the national capital on August 1. The meeting, to be held at the Constitution Club of India, will bring together experts, vehicle owners and members of the public to discuss concerns.

Article Title: NEET UG leak case: Delhi court asks CBI to appoint public prosecutor
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The special fast track court at Delhi's Rouse Avenue Courts on Monday directed the director of prosecution to appoint a public prosecutor to represent the State (CBI) in the NEET UG 2026 paper leak case. The direction came after no one appeared on behalf of the CBI during the hearing.The court subsequently adjourned the bail pleas of accused Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal to August 3.Special judge Anu Grover Baliga passed the direction while hearing the bail applications of the two accused before the newly constituted fast track court set up under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.According to news agency ANI, the proceedings marked the first hearing in the NEET UG paper leak case before the designated fast track court. However, the matter could not proceed after the absence of representation for the CBI. Advocate AP Singh appeared on behalf of the accused.The fast track court was constituted on July 23 to exclusively try offences under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, along with connected offences. All pending cases under the Act are to be transferred to the newly designated court.Earlier, on July 17, the predecessor court had sought the CBI's response to the bail applications filed by Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal.According to the CBI, Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal are among 13 accused arrested in connection with the alleged leak of the NEET UG question paper before the examination. All the accused are currently in judicial custody till August 6.The agency alleged that Mangilal Biwal contacted Shubham Khairnar to procure the NEET UG question paper for his son, Vikas Biwal. It further claimed that the leaked question paper was recovered from Mangilal Biwal's mobile phone.According to the investigation, Mangilal allegedly obtained the paper from Yash Yadav for Rs 10 lakh. During interrogation, Vikas Biwal allegedly told investigators that he had come into contact with Yash Yadav while attending coaching classes in Sikar, Rajasthan.The CBI further alleged that the leaked paper was circulated through a chain involving Shubham Khairnar, Yash Yadav, Mangilal Biwal, Vikas Biwal and Dinesh Biwal. Investigators have also alleged that Mangilal subsequently sold the leaked paper to several candidates for Rs 12 lakh each.An FIR in the case was registered on May 12, 2026, on the complaint of a government official under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.The matter will next be taken up on August 3, when the court is expected to hear the bail pleas after the prosecution enters appearance.
Article Summary: The direction came after no one appeared on behalf of the CBI during the hearing. The court subsequently adjourned the bail pleas of accused Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal to August 3. All the accused are currently in judicial custody till August 6.

Article Title: Bihar bandh violence: Siwan cop suspended for firing AK-47; 200 NEET protesters detained
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view What is your opinion on the treatment of minors during detentions? It is unacceptable, they should be protected It's necessary for maintaining order 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PATNA: Nearly 200 students allegedly detained after the July 22 and 25 protests, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak, remained in custody for over 24 hours across police stations in the city, advocates alleged. Meanwhile, a Siwan police personnel was suspended for firing AK-47 during the July 25 bandh violence.Advocate Akanksha Shahi, who is providing legal aid to several detainees, said 58 of them were sent to remand on July 25. Around 87 more are likely to be sent to judicial custody on Sunday, she said. Several detainees are minors, she added.According to advocates, around 15 detainees were held at Gandhi Maidan police station, 28 at Digha, and 22 each at Rupaspura and Airport police stations, among others.Advocate Abhishek Kumar, who is also providing pro bono legal aid (free legal help), said the families of several detainees were not informed about their detention. He said detainees are required to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours, which expired at 2pm on Sunday. The detainees were taken for medical examinations to govt hospitals around 5pm on Sunday, he said.Soma Kumari, a student activist and member of the Disha Students’ Organisation at Airport police station, said, “Over 200 people were detained during the July 25 protest.Around 70% of them are minors. Police are not informing us about the next step.”She added, “This is happening after it was assured by the govt that no action will be taken on the protesting students and all the FIRs will be quashed. But instead of quashing the FIRs, Patna police has kept them.”Families of the detainees said some students were caught while passing through the protest area.Shahi said the police were releasing all the women and minors, while other detainees were being sent to judicial custody.Responding to the allegations, Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma told TOI on Sunday that 86 protesters arrested during the July 25 violence near Gandhi Maidan were sent to judicial custody, while 60 others, including minors and women, were released on personal bonds. He said a case had been registered against the accused at Gandhi Maidan police station.The SSP added that in connection with the July 22 protest, police registered 23 FIRs across different police stations in the city and arrested 67 people, who were sent to judicial custody in different cases.Providing further details of the July 25 violence, Gandhi Maidan SHO Akhilesh Kumar Mishra, who sustained injuries during the clash, said four FIRs were registered in connection with the incident. One FIR was lodged on his statement, another on the statement of a magistrate, a third by the officer in charge of the Gandhi Maidan TOP checkpost that was attacked during the violence, and the fourth on a complaint by a repairman alleging that protesters overturned a govt vehicle parked near the police vehicle garage.Mishra said the accused have been booked under multiple charges, including unlawful assembly, rioting, attempt to murder, obstructing public servants from discharging their duties, and other offences related to the violence. Referring to the July 22 protest, Mishra said four FIRs were also registered at Gandhi Maidan police station, leading to the arrest of five people from the police station’s jurisdiction, while additional arrests were made by other police stations.Meanwhile, ADG (Law and Order) K Suhita Anupam said FIRs were registered in Saran, Siwan, Bhagalpur, Sitamarhi and Jehanabad in connection with violence during the July 25 bandh.She said 56 people were arrested in Saran, 25 in Siwan, 41 named accused in Bhagalpur, 13 in Sitamarhi and 13 in Jehanabad. She added that 19 govt vehicles and one private vehicle were vandalised, while 58 police personnel were injured, adding Siwan personnel who fired an AK-47 had been suspended.
Article Summary: Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma says 86 protesters arrested during the July 25 violence near Gandhi Maidan were sent to judicial custody. 60 others, including minors and women, were released on personal bonds. Siwan police personnel suspended for firing AK-47 during July 25 bandh violence.

Article Title: 101 murder accused among 989 with criminal records in July 20 Parliament march violence: Delhi Police
Article Text:
Delhi Police says 101 murder accused among 989 with criminal records in Parliament march violence (PTI photo)

Police: Force used only after repeated warnings ignored





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police said its investigation has revealed that 101 individuals with murder charges, 284 people booked in dacoity and robbery cases, and 92 accused in sexual assault and other offences against women and children were part of the violence during the protesters' march to Parliament on July 20.A report submitted by police commissioner Anurag Kumar to the govt details how the police examined a total of 2,873 criminals involved in attacking cops and vandalising vehicles. Of them, 989 were found to have criminal antecedents in heinous offences, it said.Action, including arrest and investigation against these individuals with criminal history is likely to continue; cases against students will be dropped, said sources.The suspects were identified using FRS cameras, along with CCTV footage and videos recorded by police personnel and the public.Several suspects were tracked in areas where the violence occurred and were seen throwing stones, attacking cops, damaging govt vehicles and vandalising public property, police said.“Probe revealed a considerable number of persons present in and around the protest sites were not merely individuals with isolated criminal antecedents but included habitual and repeat offenders, several of whom have previous involvement in grave and heinous offences such as murder, attempt to murder, dacoity/robbery, rape, offences against women, Arms Act violations, kidnapping, snatching and narcotics-related offences,” the report, accessed by TOI , said.The list also includes 61 who were involved in rape cases, 25 in molestation cases, six booked under Pocso Act, 229 under Arms Act, 135 in snatching cases, 19 in kidnapping cases and 67 in offences under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act.Of the 101 people with murder cases, 42 had been involved in two or more criminal cases, while 12 had criminal histories spanning at least 10 cases or more. Among the 62 people accused in attempt-to-murder cases, 25 had multiple criminal cases registered against them.Similarly, of the 284 people linked to dacoity and robbery, 155 had been involved in two or more criminal cases, including 31 with criminal histories spanning at least 10 cases or more. Among the rape accused, eight had been booked in multiple criminal cases. Six of the accused in molestation cases and nine of the accused in NDPSrelated offences were also found to be repeat offenders.According to the report, a permission had been granted only for a protest at Jantar Mantar and not for a march to Parliament. “However, the protesters continued to breach the barricades and reached very close to the parliament, sending its security apparatus into a tizzy,” a senior police officer said.Force was used only after repeated warnings were ignored and protesters continued to breach one barricade after another, police have said. “Even senior police officers, many of whom were assaulted and injured during the violence, exercised restraint for a considerable period before action was taken.”Apost-incident review was initiated examining the entire episode, including the role of miscreants who, police said, infiltrated the protest alongside genuine demonstrators. “Despite several police personnel sustaining injuries, the situation did not spiral completely out of control, demonstrating that the police response was marked by deliberate restraint rather than negligence,” the police said.
Article Summary: Delhi Police says 101 murder accused among 989 with criminal records in Parliament march violence. Force used only after repeated warnings ignored, police have said. Action, including arrest and investigation against individuals with criminal history is likely to continue; cases against students will be dropped.

Article Title: Missing safety shield: Bengaluru Metro death revives demand for platform doors
Article Text:
Namma Metro services on the Yellow Line were disrupted for over two hours after a passenger died by suicide at Huskur station (Representative image)





BENGALURU: A passenger's death by suicide at a Bengaluru Metro station on Monday has once again put the spotlight on the long-standing demand for platform screen doors (PSDs), even as the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (BMRCL) has no immediate plan to install them across its existing 96km network.Namma Metro services on the Yellow Line were disrupted for more than two hours after a 37-year-old passenger died by suicide by jumping in front of a moving train at Huskur station on Hosur Road around 5.50pm.Following the incident, services between Bommasandra and Electronics City were suspended.Normal services across the entire 19km Yellow Line stretch from Bommasandra to RV Road resumed around 8pm.The deceased was identified as Rajesh Hiremath, a social media content creator and resident of Anantnagar, Hebbagodi.Police said Hiremath was unmarried, originally from Raichur and lived in Bengaluru with his mother.No suicide note was found on him. Police said he had slipped into depression over job-related issues.Police further said Hiremath had worked with a YouTube channel for around a year before quitting four months ago.Hiremath came under the train arriving from Bommasandra and heading towards RV Road and succumbed to his injuries on the spot.“Upon noticing the passenger on the track, the train operator immediately applied emergency brakes and alerted the Operations Control Centre. Traction power was switched off, and station staff and Metro security personnel were mobilised. Police were also informed immediately,” BMRCL said in a statement.After the track was cleared and mandatory safety inspections were completed, traction power was restored at 7.42pm and services resumed at 8pm.BMRCL said refunds for online tickets involving curtailed journeys would be processed on Tuesday.The incident has once again revived the long-standing demand for installation of platform screen doors at Metro stations.However, BMRCL, which operates Namma Metro, has no immediate plans to install PSDs across its operational network of 96km with 83 stations.As a safety measure, BMRCL has installed steel barricades at high-footfall stations, including Majestic Interchange station, MG Road, Indiranagar, Benniganahalli and RV Road.BMRCL has already proposed installing PSDs at 177 stations, including existing operational stations, as part of the detailed project report for the proposed Hebbal-Sarjapur Metro line under Phase 3A. The project is awaiting final approval from the central government.Since the launch of Metro services in 2011, several incidents of suicide, suicide attempts and accidental falls have been reported on the network.Between 2012 and 2025, four passengers died by suicide after jumping in front of moving trains at Metro stations.At least 16 passengers attempted suicide, while there were 23 incidents of unauthorised entry onto tracks and seven cases of passengers accidentally falling onto tracks.In July this year, two suicide-related incidents were reported, including the fatal incident at Huskur station.In the earlier incident, a woman who jumped onto the track at Rajajinagar station was rescued by security staff.Metro commuters have long been demanding the installation of PSDs to prevent suicide attempts and accidental falls onto tracks.“Passengers have been demanding for years that BMRCL install PSDs, but the corporation has not taken immediate steps. BMRCL should take measures to prevent such incidents in future. Such matters also cause major inconvenience to commuters,” said Sreenath, a Metro user.BMRCL chief public relations officer BL Yeshwanth Chavan said steel barricades had been installed at high-footfall stations as a precautionary measure.“At present, steel barricades have been installed at high-footfall stations as a precautionary measure. These help in maintaining passenger queues and preventing accidental falls onto tracks. As part of future Metro network expansion plans, there are proposals to install platform screen doors at both existing and upcoming stations.”
Article Summary: Namma Metro services on the Yellow Line were disrupted for over two hours after a passenger died by suicide at Huskur station. The deceased was identified as Rajesh Hiremath, a social media content creator and resident of Anantnagar, Hebbagodi. Police said he had slipped into depression over job-related issues. Metro commuters have long been demanding the installation of platform screen doors.

Article Title: Throat slit in park, woman types last words on phone that help cops nab boyfriend
Article Text:
Police arrested Ritesh Rajwade, 23, who confessed to the brutal crime.





RAIPUR: A 20-year-old domestic worker, her throat slit in a brutal attack inside a public park in Chhattisgarh's Surajpur district, desperately ran out in search of help before collapsing in a puddle of blood. Unable to speak because of the deep neck wound, she communicated basic details about herself by typing on a mobile phone shortly before she died, helping police crack the case within hours.Speaking to TOI, Surajpur SP Yogesh Patel said, "Police have arrested a man identified as Ritesh Rajwade, 23, on charges of murder. The man confessed to the crime claiming that he was in relationship with her for past six years and was upset after she went cold. It's not clear if it was a consensual meeting."As per the initial investigators it appears that the attack stemmed from a relationship dispute after the accused allegedly suspected the victim of having another affair.The victim, Radhika Rajwade, a native of Latori village, worked as a domestic help at a residence in Surajpur town.According to preliminary probe, Ritesh had called Radhika to Nehru Park on Sunday evening.CCTV footage and the investigation suggest the two spent nearly an hour talking inside the park before an argument broke out.The accused pulled out a knife and slashed Radhika's throat. The blade pierced through her neck. Believing she had been fatally injured, the accused pulled the knife out and fled on his motorcycle.Gravely wounded but still conscious, Radhika staggered out of the park in a desperate bid to save herself. Bleeding profusely and unable to cry for help, she ran several metres before collapsing. Shocked passerby rushed to her aid and shifted her to the district hospital.Doctors found her unable to speak because of the severity of the neck injury. Police officials who reached the hospital attempted to question her. She reportedly gestured repeatedly towards the officers, asking for a mobile phone. Realising she wanted to communicate, they handed her one.She was later referred to Ambikapur medical college hospital but she succumbed to injuries late night.With the victim's identification of the accused and CCTV footage from the park and surrounding roads, police pieced together the sequence of events. Technical evidence, including the victim's phone records and chats, corroborated the lead, following which Ritesh was traced and arrested the same night from a forest area.Police are also trying to recover the weapon used in the crime and are examining digital evidence to establish the exact sequence leading to the murder.The incident has shocked residents of Surajpur town as the attack took place at Nehru Park, a popular public space barely 500 metres from the Kotwali police station, raising concerns over safety in the heart of the town.
Article Summary: Police arrest Ritesh Rajwade, 23, who confessed to the brutal crime. The victim, Radhika, was unable to speak because of the deep neck wound. She communicated basic details about herself by typing on a mobile phone shortly before she died.

Article Title: 'Allah commanded me': Knife-wielding man attacks 3 women on Paris street - video
Article Text: Panic gripped a busy Paris street on Monday after a man armed with two kitchen knives attacked three women in broad daylight before being overpowered by bystanders and an off-duty police officer.Two of the victims suffered severe injuries, while investigators are yet to establish the suspect's whereabouts or motive.French interior minister Laurent Nunez told reporters that the suspect attacked three women aged 19, 24 and 36 with two kitchen knives. "The man had been detained by an off-duty police officer. I pay tribute to him, it was a courageous act," Nunez said.Paris police said the attack took place at around 11:30 am local time (0930 GMT). All three victims were taken to hospital following the incident.The suspect's identity and motive remain unclear. Nunez said police had been unable to verify his identity and described his statements during arrest as 'incoherent'.Video footage first posted on Snapchat and later verified by Reuters showed a man with long black hair, wearing a cream tracksuit and wielding a large knife in each hand, attempting to attack and stab a young woman.It was not immediately clear whether the woman was injured.Another video showed the suspect lying on the ground after being restrained by members of the public, with the two knives visible nearby on a pedestrian crossing.Mohamed-Ali Bouhadjar, 26, who filmed the incident and shared the footage on Snapchat, described how bystanders intervened."When I saw him stab a woman in the back, I started shouting, 'Come on, let's stop him!' Several people stepped in," Bouhadjar told Reuters."One person threw a suitcase at him. He dropped the knives. At that moment, I grabbed him, swept his legs out from under him, and we pinned him to the ground," he said.The footage also captured the suspect making a religious statement while being restrained. "It is Allah who commanded me," the man lying on the floor says in the video.Authorities have not linked the attack to terrorism. Nunez said the motive remained unknown and reiterated that investigators were still working to establish the suspect's identity.The French national anti-terrorist prosecutor's office said it was 'in observation' over whether to open a formal investigation into the attack.The incident comes two days after an Islamist radical drove a rented minivan into a Pride parade in Berlin, killing one woman and injuring 29 others.
Article Summary: A man armed with two kitchen knives attacked three women in broad daylight in Paris. Two of the victims suffered severe injuries, while investigators are yet to establish the suspect's whereabouts or motive. The suspect's identity and motive remain unclear. The incident comes two days after an Islamist radical drove a rented minivan into a Pride parade in Berlin.

Article Title: CJP protest in Mumbai: Cop ‘inappropriately touches’ woman in video, stirs row
Article Text:
The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.





MUMBAI: A viral video from the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Thursday, showing a policeman allegedly inappropriately touching a woman protester, stirred up a fresh controversy on Friday, with the opposition demanding his dismissal.The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.DCP (operations) Akbar Pathan said, “The official was trying to hold on to a male protester and a lady stepped in while he was looking away. Senior officers have verified all the facts and minutely assessed the video to ascertain the facts,” he said.Another police official said, “Since the video went viral late Thursday night, our senior cyber crime experts carefully zoomed in on the footage, verified it, and found that there was no misconduct.”The controversy came a day after another viral video showed a police constable, who was working as a driver, allegedly threatening young protesters that drugs would be planted on them and their career would be ruined if they continued participating in protests.The latest video quickly went viral on social media, with several opposition politicians demanding action against the policeman. Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded an apology from CM Devendra Fadnavis and dismissal of the policeman.In a post on X, Sapkal said, “The one who calls himself Devabhaau has turned out to be Duryodhan! Devabhaau’s police have become so rogue that they are violating the modesty of female students the age of their own daughters.”Mumbai Congress president and MP Varsha Gaikwad said, “What happened to a girl during the protest in Mumbai is deeply painful and disturbing. It is wrong to speak of the ‘Ladki Bahin’ scheme while treating young women in such a manner. It is a matter of shame that women are allegedly being mistreated in the land of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. False cases are being registered against students, and they are being threatened. ”Congress has organised statewide candlelight marches and ‘satyagraha’ in Maharashtra on Saturday to express solidarity with the protesting students.
Article Summary: The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage. The controversy came a day after another viral video showed a police constable, who was working as a driver, allegedly threatening young protesters.

Article Title: 3 years on, SIT probe complete in just 10% of Manipur riot cases
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.
Article Summary: Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives. Only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by state police. CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.

Article Title: 'Ab aayega aur maza!' CJP says 'time is ticking' as farmers announce march to Jantar Mantar on Sunday
Article Text:
CJP's Saurav Das alleges tanks being transported to Delhi

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das on Saturday urged the Centre to accept the protesters' demands, alleging that the government was transporting tanks to Delhi while the student agitation continued."Ab aayega aur maza! The government must understand that it can either bomb the peaceful protesters using the tanks it is transporting to Delhi (I mean, what are they trying to do by transporting these? Kill their own children? Is this where we have come in Gandhi's India?) Or, accept demands. The time is ticking!" Das said in a post on X.He made the remarks while sharing a post by the Bharatiya Kisan Union announcing that it would join the ongoing student protest at Jantar Mantar.The development comes as CJP reiterated that it may adopt a "tough stance" if the Centre does not clarify its position on the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Speaking to reporters, CJP activist Ashutosh Ranka said the meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh was constructive, but added that the organisation was still awaiting the government's response to its primary demand."Yesterday's meeting yielded a positive response regarding compensation and legal matters, reaching an in-principle agreement. We hope to receive that written agreement today. However, no concrete decision has been made regarding our main demand. Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.""Mainstream media reports suggest sources are saying Pradhan will not step down. If he does not resign, the government should state it clearly, as there is no point in continuing these meetings. We will then decide on our next steps. If the government continues this approach, we will be forced to take a tough stance," Ranka said.Earlier, activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh after the Union government gave a written assurance on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said strict action would be taken against those responsible for the alleged paper leaks. Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das urged the Centre to accept the protesters' demands. Article Title: 'Intense, highly unpredictable': Over 200,000 evacuated as massive wildfires engulf Spain, France
Article Text:
Spain, France battle devastating wildfires

More than 200,000 people have either fled or been ordered to remain indoors as massive wildfires swept across Spain and France on Friday.The fires prompted Spain to declare a national emergency, while French authorities ordered the complete evacuation, by land and sea, of one of the country's most popular holiday destinations.Authorities in south-west France ordered the evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic coast "village by village" as an "intense, highly unpredictable" wildfire scorched more than 19,000 hectares (47,000 acres) of forest.In Spain, the government declared its first-ever national emergency over a wildfire after two major blazes merged outside Madrid, while a third fire was close to joining them amid extreme heat and tinder-dry conditions across much of southern Europe.Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso described the blaze as the "worst fire in the history of the region", saying the area was facing a "perfect storm" of high temperatures, relentless winds and converging fire fronts.Local emergency services said the wildfires were advancing towards the municipalities of Robledo de Chavela and Fresnedillas de la Oliva, about 50 kilometres (31 miles) from the Spanish capital."The wildfire is at its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain," Carlos Novillo, the Madrid regional government's emergency management chief, said, as cited by the BBC."It's not possible to attack the fire in that area, so defensive measures are being taken," he added.A national emergency, which allows Spain's central government to assume powers and responsibilities normally held by the country's autonomous regions, has been declared only once before — during the nationwide blackout in April 2025.In south-west France, around 200,000 people have been evacuated as wildfires tore through the Gironde and Landes regions.In the early hours of Saturday, authorities ordered the precautionary evacuation of four towns near Bordeaux: Saint-Médard-en-Jalles, Saint-Jean-d'Illac, Martignas-sur-Jalles and Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc. According to Le Monde, the four municipalities have a combined population of about 58,400.In 2022, a wildfire in south-west France scorched more than 30,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of 50,000 people. Fueled by dry conditions and strong winds, the latest blazes have swept through coastal pine forests, with flames reaching up to 10 metres (30 feet) high.French president Emmanuel Macron said he had activated the European Union's civil protection mechanism as the country battled multiple wildfires after enduring three successive heatwaves since May.Scientists say climate change is making extreme weather events more frequent and more intense by drying out soils and waterways, fuelling wildfires and contributing to thousands of excess deaths. Europe is warming at nearly twice the global average rate.
Article Summary: Spanish government declares first-ever national emergency over wildfire. French authorities order complete evacuation of one of country's most popular holiday destinations. More than 200,000 people either fled or were ordered to remain indoors as wildfires swept across Spain and France on Friday.

Article Title: Romania F-16 shoots down drone after airspace breach
Article Text: A Romanian F-16 fighter jet shot down a drone that breached the country's airspace, Romanian President Nicusor Dan said on Friday.
Article Summary: A Romanian F-16 fighter jet shot down a drone that breached the country's airspace, Romanian President Nicusor Dan said on Friday. The drone had been in Romania's airspace for more than a week, Dan said. The Romanian military says it is investigating the incident.
